content.title: Masters 2026 leaderboard, scores: Rory McIlroy tied entering final round at Augusta
content.text: Updated April 11, 2026, 8:06 p.m. ETThe race for the green jacket at the 2026 Masters continued Saturday after the field narrowed on Friday.Rory McIlroy had quickly turned it into a historic one-man race through the first two days, but he started the third round with a bogey and needed to make some adjustments early.Things changed late in Round 3. It seemed as if McIlroy was going to continue to run away with it, but a double-bogey at the No. 11 hole and following miscues allowed Cameron Young to reach the top of the leaderboard.Young came back down eight strokes to overtake the Masters leaderboard in Round 3. Young finished with a 7-under 65. He is now 11-under and completed the round with a share of the lead.After shooting a 7-under par during Friday's second round, McIlroy's bid for a second consecutive win at Augusta National was alive and well. But after dropping a 1-over 73, things are a bit more tenuous as he no longer has full control of the leaderboard.USA TODAY covered the Masters leaderboard with the latest updates, biggest moments and highest stakes. Here is everything to know about the third round Saturday. Masters leaderboard liveThese are the top contenders as the third round is underway:T1. Cameron Young: -11 (F)T1. Rory McIlroy -11 (F)3. Sam Burns: -10 (F)4. Shane Lowry: -9 (F)T5. Jason Day: -8 (F)T5. Justin Rose: -8 (F)T7. Haotong Li: -7 (F)T7. Scottie Scheffler: -7 (F)Check out the full leaderboard here. Rory McIlroy, Cameron Young share lead going into final dayRory McIlroy and Cameron Young will share the lead entering the final round of the tournament on Sunday. McIlroy finished one shot over par of 72 for the third round, which kept the door open for someone to catch up to the 2025 champion.Young finished the round 7-under, allowing him to briefly sit atop the leaderboard alone late Saturday evening.The two golfers will likely make up the final group and close out the tournament on Sunday. Sam Burns is third on the leaderboard, just one shot behind the leaders. Rory McIlroy tries to retake leadRory McIlroy briefly took sole possession of the lead from Cameron Young at the 15th hole at 12-under. McIlroy's lead was short-lived, having moved back to 11-under after the 16th hole.He is looking to become the first back-to-back winner of the Masters since 2002. Cameron Young scoreCameron Young finished with a score of 65 after the third round, sharing the lead with Rory McIlroy at 11-under as of 6:07 p.m. ET."I feel that I have been around the lead in major champs for a few years now, but never here," Young told CBS Sports' Jim Nantz after finishing the third round. "... I'm really excited to play golf tomorrow. It's been great and I've been playing good golf the last few weeks, and grateful to do it here." Jason Day finishes 8-underJason Day finished his Round 3 with a 68 score. He sits at No. 5 on the leaderboard having shot 8-under par. Rory McIlroy not done, birdies No. 14Rory McIlroy may have had his lead overtaken but he wasn't done for the day. He worked to get right back to where he started the round, at the top. McIlroy birdied No. 14 to get back to the top spot, tying with Cameron Young for No. 1 on the leaderboard at 11-under. Cameron Young score (as of 6:07 p.m. ET)Cameron Young finished his Round 3 as the sole leader of the Masters with a 65 score at 11-under. Sam Burns moves into second place tie with McIlroySam Burns is tied with Rory McIlroy at second after he connected on a 13th hole birdie. Shane Lowry creeping towards top spotRory McIlroy's shortcomings opened the doors for others to grab the top spot. Shane Lowry is slowly creeping in. He birdied at the 14th hole to move within two strokes of the lead. Cameron Young takes command of leaderboardCameron Young overtook the leaderboard after Rory McIlroy's misfires continue in the 12th hole. Young leads at 11-under, while McIlroy sits at 10-under, solo at second place. Cameron Young ties Rory McIlroy in 16thCameron Young was down eight strokes but after the 16th hole he climbed his way to back to tie Rory McIlroy for the lead at 11-under. Cameron Young score (as of 5:35 p.m. ET)Cameroun Young has been marching his way up the ladder, as Rory McIlroy's slippage leaves hope for Young, or someone, to upend McIlroy on the leaderboard. Rory McIlroy double-bogey, leaves leaderboard up for grabsRory McIlroy left some room for another golfer to take his place on the leaderboard. A double-bogey brought McIlroy down to 11-under after No. 11 hole. Haotong Li takes one into the lakeHaotong Li misfired on a putt and he took a golf ball into a lake at Augusta National Golf Club. He found the water just minutes after Cameron Young and Rory McIlroy did so, too. Jason Day score (as of 5:25 p.m. ET)Jason Day has charted up the leaderboard. He is tied with Haotong Li for third at 9-under through 15 holes. Haotong Li is solo in thirdHaotong Li took over No. 3 spot on leaderboard, now at 9-under after 14 holes. Rory McIlroy score (as of 5:10 p.m. ET)Rory McIlroy birdies No. 10 to take a two shot lead at 13-under par. Cameron Young chasing Rory McIlroyCameron Young moved within one stroke of Rory McIlroy following his No. 14 hole performance. Young is 11-under through 14 holes in Round 3. Jason Day score (as of 5:02 p.m. ET)Jason Day has climbed his way into the leaderboard with three birdies in a row. Day is tied at No. 5 with Sam Burns at 8-under. Shane Lowry birdies No. 10Shane Lowry jumped to a tie for third after his No. 10 birdie. Cameron Young moves up to No. 2Cameron Young after the 13th hole. Young is currently at 10-under, two strokes behind McIlroy for top gun. Scottie Scheffler finishes round 7-underThrough 18 holes in Round 3, Scottie Scheffler finished 7-under with a 65 score. The two-time Masters champion is tied at 6th with Patrick Reed. Shane Lowry climbs the chartsShane Lowry still on a high from his ace shot, birdied the No. 8 hole and moved to 9-under for a three-way tie with Cameron Young and Haotong Li. Cameron Young on a mission, fifth birdieCameron Young is on fire. He chipped in his fifth birdie at the 10th hole. He jumped into a tie for second at 9-under. Russell Henley score (as of 4:05 p.m. ET)Russell Henley finished his round with a birdie, jumping into the leaderboard's top 10. He scored a 66 and finished 6-under par. Haotong Li jumps to second with eagleHaotong Li leaped into second place, connecting on an eagle putt in the eighth. Collin Morikawa eagled the 14th holeCollin Morikawa teed off the 14th hole sending the golf ball 94 feet to land an eagle shot. Patrick Reed drops to fifth-placePatrick Reed missed a birdie at the fifth hole, which dropped him to 7-under, leaving the four-way tie at second, dropping to a tie at No. 5 on the leaderboard with Haotong Li. Cameron Young score (as of 3:50 p.m. ET)Cameron Young made a jump to second-place tie after No. 8. He joined Shane Lowry, Sam Burns and Patrick Reed at 8-under. Shane Lowry jumps to second with hole-in-oneWhether skill, or a little luck of the Irish, Shane Lowry jumped into a tie at second with Sam Burns and Patrick Reed after sinking a hole-in-one at No. 6. Sam Burns score (as of 3:35 p.m. ET)Working his way to the top of the leaderboard, Sam Burns is at 8-under through three holes. He is tied second with Patrick Reed. Patrick Reed birdies on No. 3Patrick Reed moved to two strokes behind first place with a birdie at the third hole. Justin Rose score (as of 3:15 p.m. ET)Steady as he goes as Rose starts Saturday par, par and is still at 5-under for the tournament. Wyndham Clark eagles on moving dayClark remains one golfer looking to put some pressure on Rory McIlroy. His eagle on three was as clean as they come. Rory McIlroy score (as of 3:05 p.m. ET)Rory McIlroy had a messy start to the third round, hitting his drive just right of the bunker on one. He ended up with a bogey to kick things off. He heads to two to attempt to steady any jitters. McIroy is now -11 on the tournament. Patrick Reed score (as of 2:55 p.m. ET)Patrick Reed cut into Rory McIlroy's with an immediate birdie to kick off his round. He is now 7-under on the tournament. Scottie Scheffler score (as of 2:50 p.m. ET)Scottie Scheffler’s fourth birdie of the round at No. 11 moves him firmly into contention, joining the group tied for third at 6-under as he heads to No. 12. Cameron Young score (as of 2:47 p.m. ET)Cameron Young vaults into a tie for second with back-to-back birdies, reaching 6-under through four holes. Scottie Scheffler score (as of 2:23 p.m. ET)Scottie Scheffler is heating up, rattling off three consecutive birdies at Nos. 7, 8, and 9 to reach 5-under through the front nine. Chris Gotterup score (as of 2:18 p.m. ET)Chris Gotterup moves into a tie for fourth after an eagle at No. 2 and a par at No. 3. He sits at 5-under through three holes, joining Tommy Fleetwood, Justin Rose, and Shane Lowry in the group. Scottie Scheffler score (as of 2 p.m. ET)Scottie Scheffler continues to build momentum, picking up a birdie at No. 7 to move to 3-under and into a tie for 15th. Matt Fitzpatrick score (as of 1:45 p.m. ET)Matt Fitzpatrick is climbing the leaderboard, with early birdies at Nos. 2 and 4 moving him to 3-under through four holes and into a tie for 13th. Scottie Scheffler score (as of 1:14 p.m. ET)Scottie Scheffler's eagle at No. 2, his second of the week, moves him to 2-under and into a tie for 16th as he makes his way to the 5th hole. Scottie Scheffler score (as of 12:41 p.m. ET)Scottie Scheffler is underway in his third round at Augusta National, opening with a par at No. 1 hole. He remains even as he heads to the second hole. Sepp Straka score (as of 12:25 p.m. ET)Sepp Straka is off to a strong start, picking up back-to-back birdies at Nos. 2 and 3. He sits at 1-under through five holes, tied for 20th. Scottie Scheffler tees off in 15 minutesWorld No. 1 Scottie Scheffler tees off at 12:16 p.m. ET in the third round at Augusta National, paired with Ludvig Åberg. After a second-round 74, Scheffler sits at even par and tied for 24th, with plenty of ground to make up on Saturday. Brian Harman score (as of 11:26 a.m. ET)Brian Harman is climbing the leaderboard with three birdies through his third round, at Nos. 2, 4, and 6. He sits at 1-over through seven holes, tied for 32nd. Jon Rahm score (as of 11 a.m. ET)Jon Rahm got off to a strong start in his third round, picking up birdies at Nos. 1 and 3. He stumbled with a bogey at No. 5 and currently sits at 3-over through five holes. The third round at the Masters is underwayKurt Kitayama and Alex Noren have officially started their third-round pairing, and Saturday's action is now in full swing!How to watch Masters: TV channel, streaming SaturdayAll main feed coverage for all four days can also be found on Masters.com and the Masters App.Paramount+: Noon-2 p.m. ETCBS/Paramount+: 2-7 p.m. ETWatch the 2026 Masters from Augusta with FuboMasters tee times todayAll times Eastern9:31 a.m.: Kurt Kitayama and Alex Noren9:42 a.m.: Charl Schwartzel and Rasmus Hojgaard9:53 a.m.: Jon Rahm and Si Woo Kim10:04 a.m.: Brian Harman and Corey Conners10:15 a.m.: Sergio Garcia and Maverick McNealy10:26 a.m.: Keegan Bradley and Viktor Hovland10:37 a.m.: Justin Thomas and Gary Woodland10:48 a.m.: Samuel Stevens and Adam Scott11:10 a.m.: Marco Penge and Matt McCarty11:21 a.m.: Jordan Spieth and Sepp Straka11:32 a.m.: Aaron Rai and Jacob Bridgeman11:43 a.m.: Patrick Cantlay and Sungjae Im11:54 a.m.: Dustin Johnson and Russell Henley12:05 p.m.: Harris English and Ryan Gerard12:16 p.m.: Ludvig Aberg and Scottie Scheffler12:38 p.m.: Collin Morikawa and Brian Campbell12:49 p.m.: Nick Taylor and Matt Fitzpatrick1 p.m.: Hideki Matsuyama and Michael Brennan1:11 p.m.: Jake Knapp and Xander Schauffele1:22 p.m.: Ben Griffin and Max Homa1:33 p.m.: Chris Gotterup and Brooks Koepka1:55 p.m.: Jason Day and Cameron Young2:06 p.m.: Haotong Li and Kristoffer Reitan2:17 p.m.: Wyndham Clark and Tyrrell Hatton2:28 p.m.: Shane Lowry and Tommy Fleetwood2:39 p.m.: Patrick Reed and Justin Rose2:50 p.m.: Rory McIlroy and Sam Burns Masters odds: Updated Favorites at AugustaAll odds via BetMGM on Thursday evening, April 9.Favorites1. Rory McIlroy (+280)2. Scottie Scheffler (+400)3. Xander Schauffele (+1000)4. Sam Burns (+1200) Masters predictions and picksHere are some predictions made ahead of the Masters.Will Cheney, Augusta Chronicle: Justin Rose's experience will help himCheney writes, "(Rose has) lost in a pair of Masters playoffs (Sergio Garcia in 2017 and Rory McIlroy in 2025). Experience plays here and this will be his 21st start at Augusta. It would only be fitting to see McIlroy put the green jacket on Rose early Sunday evening; playoff, or no playoff."Ross Kelly, CBS Sports: Ludvig Aberg will struggleKelly noted that the model CBS Sports uses predicted a shockingly poor finish for Ludvig Aberg despite him being a pre-tournament favorite.Kelly writes, "The 26-year-old has already racked up five worldwide wins in his career and he's finished solo second and solo seventh in two career starts at Augusta National. However, he's down to No. 17 in the Official World Golf Ranking after peaking at No. 4 last year because of a string of bad starts late last season and early in 2026. He's also missed the cut in four of his eight career major championship starts and an afternoon-morning stagger on Thursday and Friday is likely to have him playing in firmer and faster conditions than most."Matt Barrie, ESPN: Jon Rahm to winBarrie writes, "He has quietly been playing some of the best golf in the world this season. He's in a great spot personally and professionally. And his recent form will awake the roars at Augusta National this week."Rahm has not looked great early on at Augusta. Through six holes, he was already at 3-over. Rahm certainly has the talent to bounce back, but it has been a rough start for the 2023 green jacket winner.Golfweek: Brooks Koepka (+220 to miss the cut)Nick Stavas writes ahead of the Masters, "I like Brooks Koepka and I think his overall game is trending in the right direction, but his putting has been abysmal this season and that doesn't bode well for Augusta. Koepka's record has been feast or famine at the Masters, with three top-10s and three missed cuts in his last seven starts. Unless he really turns things around with the flatstick, I fear he'll be sent packing Friday." Masters predictions: Sleeper picks at AugustaUSA TODAY Sports' Jon Hoefling offered up a trio of sleepers plus one intriguing long shot who have the talent to buck the odds and put on a green jacket if things break their way ahead of the first round.Tommy Fleetwood (+2200)Fleetwood is someone who often gets glossed over when discussing the best golfers in the world, but he's been consistently good at Augusta the last eight years, finishing in the top-25 in five of those tournaments, including a tie for third place in 2024. He tends to play up at Augusta and is fresh off winning the Tour Championship in 2025.Patrick Reed (+3300)Patrick Reed won the Masters back in 2018, so he knows what it takes to get the green jacket. Of course, his presence on the LIV Tour for the last few years certainly hasn't helped his chances. He might be a little too used to playing in three-day tournaments at this point. However, Reed is different.In the seven Masters Tournaments since his victory, he's finished top-12 or better in five of them, and that includes a top-10 finish in three of his last five Masters appearances. A bet on Reed to finish in the top-20 could pay out massively.Jordan Spieth (+3300)It's been just over 10 years since Spieth won the green jacket at Augusta, and he's been inconsistent ever since. Five years ago, he tied for third. Four years ago, he missed the cut. Three years ago, he tied for fourth. Two years ago, he missed the cut. Last year, he tied for 14th.Sure, the pattern would indicate that he's due for some regression in 2026, but streaks are meant to be broken and Spieth has played in this tournament enough to warrant some confidence that he can still do well. After all, he's finished top-25 in more than half of the events he's played this year.Masters location: Where is Augusta National?The 90th edition of the Masters Tournament will get underway this week, and for the 90th iteration in a row, it will take place at the same golf course in Georgia.Augusta National Golf Club has hosted every Masters Tournament dating back to the first one in 1934. That makes Augusta National (and the Masters) unique among golf majors. No other major tournament – those being the U.S. Open, PGA Championship and British Open – has taken place exclusively at the same golf club. — Jack McKessy How many courses are at Augusta National?Augusta National Golf Club has just two courses (or one-and-a-half, depending on how you look at it). The Masters will take place on the club's iconic 18 holes. Wednesday is a slight departure for the Par 3 competition, which will take place at the nine-hole Par 3 course. How much does it cost to play Augusta National?While there are no green fees for the course, the fact comes with a major caveat. Augusta National is a private club, which means the only way to play is by being a member (or a guest of one), being an employee of the club, or by qualifying for the Masters. You choose which is more feasible. How to become a member at Augusta National Golf Club?If you'd like to land a membership at Augusta National Golf Club, you'd better start networking. There is no application process, with membership an invite-only process. The club has a long history of privacy, and while many reports have listed the total number of members around 300, there is no exact number confirmed by Augusta National.Once you secure the remarkably exclusive invitation, you'd better make sure you can afford to actually accept it. A range of reports over the last 15 years have placed the initiation fee at somewhere between $40,000 and $300,000, while annual dues are estimated to run between $4,000 and $30,000. — USA TODAY has more Food at the MastersThree items have slightly increased in price this year. The blueberry muffin and southern cheese straws are both up to $2.50 from $2 a year ago, and cookies are now up to $2, a 25-cent increase from last year.However, all the other traditional Augusta National staples will stay at the same prices as they were in 2025. In fact, the price of the egg salad and pimento cheese sandwiches hasn't increased since 2002.Egg Salad: $1.50Pimento Cheese: $1.50Masters Club: $3Pork Bar-B-Que: $3Chicken Salad on Honey Wheat: $3Ham & Cheese on Rye: $3Georgia Peach Ice Cream Sandwich: $3Beverages, too, remain the same as last year.Soft drinks: $2Iced tea/bottled water: $2Beer/wine: $6 Masters Tournament 2026: How to watch, TV channel, live streamPrime Video makes its debut as a Masters broadcaster this year and will carry the event for the first time ever with two hours of streaming coverage for the first and second rounds. ESPN will provide linear cable coverage for those two days, picking up where Amazon Prime leaves off.On the weekend, CBS will again handle the main feed for The Masters. The first two hours of coverage on Saturday and Sunday will air exclusively on Paramount+, before the network takes over for the remainder of each round.All main feed coverage for all four days can also be found on Masters.com and the Masters App. Here's a breakdown of the main broadcast schedule for the 2026 Masters:Watch The Masters on Prime VideoAll times Eastern.Saturday and Sunday (April 11-12)Paramount+: 12-2 p.m.CBS/Paramount+: 2-7 p.m.
